# Ghost Workers Compensation Insurance

> Specialized ghost policy workers compensation insurance for employers facing audit risk, ghost employee liability, and payroll misclassification — by Contractors Choice Agency.

We provide workers compensation insurance for employers whose employees misrepresent their job classification, go unreported, or where payroll fraud creates audit exposure. Our ghost policy specialists have 20+ years of experience and are licensed in all 50 states.

A "ghost workers comp policy" (ghost policy) is a legitimate, carrier-issued workers compensation policy where the employer is listed but no employees are covered at issuance. It satisfies state licensing requirements and contract certificate demands without covering a current workforce.

## Core Insurance Products

- [Ghost Workers Compensation Policy](https://ghostworkerscompensationinsurance.com/services/ghost-workers-compensation): Ghost policy insurance for employers who need proof of WC coverage — satisfies licensing and contract requirements
- [Workers Comp Audit Protection](https://ghostworkerscompensationinsurance.com/services/audit-protection): Coverage defending against retroactive audit assessments and premium deficits when payroll is found to exceed estimates
- [Employer Liability Insurance](https://ghostworkerscompensationinsurance.com/services/employer-liability): Part B coverage protecting employers when injured employees sue directly outside the workers comp system
- [Payroll Fraud & Ghost Employee Coverage](https://ghostworkerscompensationinsurance.com/services/payroll-fraud): Protection when employees misrepresent their job class, go unreported, or are paid off-books
- [Independent Contractor Misclassification Insurance](https://ghostworkerscompensationinsurance.com/services/independent-contractor): Defense coverage for employers who misclassified employees as 1099 contractors
- [Multi-State Workers Comp Coverage](https://ghostworkerscompensationinsurance.com/services/multi-state-coverage): Ghost policies across all 50 states including monopolistic state compliance
